INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.

A firm produced its goods at an average cost of $14. It then produces the same output at a lower average cost by different methods of production. The price remains above the marginal cost. In which ways is this firm now more efficient? allocative dynamic efficiency efficiency

options.A: no no
options.B: no yes
options.C: yes no
options.D: yes yes

questions.questionText: In 2008 Beijing held the Olympic Games and built a new stadium and infrastructure. 1.5 million people lost their homes and were relocated far away from their communities. Factories were closed during the games to reduce air pollution. Today, the stadium is a major tourist attraction and the athletes’ accommodation is used as apartments. For which group is the likely excess of marginal social benefit over marginal social cost the greatest?

options.A: construction workers who built the site
options.B: factory workers who returned to their jobs after the games
options.C: residents who were rehoused far away from Beijing
options.D: those who live in the former athletes’ accommodation

questions.questionText: The graph shows the budget line for a household as used in indifference curve analysis. good Y R S T O good X What can be concluded about the amount of income that could be spent by the household?

options.A: It is greater at point R than point S.
options.B: It is greater at point T than point S.
options.C: It is greatest at point S.
options.D: It is the same at points R, S and T.

questions.questionText: Which act of purchase or consumption is most likely to illustrate the law of diminishing marginal utility?

options.A: the final course of an ‘eat all you can’ banquet to end an evening out
options.B: the last coin to complete an enthusiast’s coin collection
options.C: the second of the two rolls of wallpaper needed to decorate a room
options.D: the tenth driving lesson needed to enable a learner to pass the driving test

questions.questionText: A kinked demand curve is often used when economists attempt to analyse the way in which oligopolists operate. What does the kinked demand curve indicate?

options.A: Oligopolists are unable to achieve profit maximisation.
options.B: Satisficing is the best objective for firms that operate under conditions of oligopoly.
options.C: There are always benefits available for oligopolists if they reduce price, but not if they increase it.
options.D: There is a tendency towards price stability when firms operate under conditions of oligopoly.

questions.questionText: Why might a firm adopt a policy of diversification?

options.A: to achieve cost economies of scale
options.B: to agree common prices with rivals
options.C: to ensure greater ability to spread investment risks
options.D: to increase productivity of labour

questions.questionText: What would be likely to help a small firm to survive and what might be a threat to its survival? help threat

options.A: contestability of the market expensive new technology
options.B: customers valuing personal service new government regulations on its business
options.C: low barriers to entering its industry managerial diseconomies of scale
options.D: selling a homogeneous product new firms entering the market

options.A: JM B JK C JM  OQ D JK  OQ

questions.questionText: What identifies the output level required to meet the stated aim of a monopoly firm? aim of firm produce at output where

options.A: maximum efficiency marginal cost is at a minimum
options.B: profit maximising marginal cost is equal to average revenue
options.C: quantity of sales maximising marginal revenue is equal to average cost
options.D: revenue maximising marginal revenue is zero

questions.questionText: A government implements three economic policies.
When there are positive externalities in consumption, what can be concluded about the output of the market?

options.A: Output must be above the allocative efficient level.
options.B: Output must be at the allocative efficient level.
options.C: Output must be below the allocative efficient level.
options.D: Output can be above or below the allocative efficient level.

questions.questionText: The Gini coefficient of a country is 0.40. The poorest income earners in this country pay no income tax. The government increases the tax rate on the highest income earners, which results in a more even distribution of income. What could be concluded from this?

options.A: The Gini coefficient falls and the income tax system becomes more progressive.
options.B: The Gini coefficient falls and the income tax system becomes more regressive.
options.C: The Gini coefficient rises and the income tax system becomes more progressive.
options.D: The Gini coefficient rises and the income tax system becomes more regressive.

questions.questionText: What is meant by economic rent?

options.A: any amount above the minimum earnings required to keep labour in its current job
options.B: the marginal physical product of labour multiplied by marginal revenue
options.C: the minimum amount required to keep labour in its current job
options.D: the regular payment to a property owner in exchange for the use of a building

questions.questionText: A firm operates under perfect competition in both product and factor markets with labour as the only variable factor input. In the diagram, the line JK shows the relationship between the marginal physical product of labour and the hours worked. J marginal physical product of labour 8 (units) K 0 1 2 3 4 5 thousand hours When the marginal revenue of the product is $1.60, the firm uses 3000 hours of labour. What is the hourly wage?
A government attempts to stimulate growth by cutting its main interest rate. What might reduce the effectiveness of this?

options.A: if investors’ expectations are rising
options.B: if more borrowing is taking place
options.C: if savings are falling
options.D: if the marginal propensity to consume is falling

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the relative position of two countries X and Y on a Kuznets curve. inequality X Y O income per head What does the diagram indicate?

options.A: Country X collects more income tax than country Y.
options.B: Country X has a higher national income than country Y.
options.C: Country Y has less income inequality than country X.
options.D: Country Y is less economically developed than country X.

questions.questionText: The Measure of Economic Welfare (MEW) is often regarded as a better measure of economic welfare than Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per head. What is additionally included in the calculation for MEW?

options.A: the cost of paid work
options.B: the cost of producing armaments
options.C: the estimated cost of damage to the environment
options.D: the negative impact on the shadow economy

questions.questionText: Which statement about national income accounting is correct?

options.A: Depreciation does not need to be subtracted from GDP figures because it has already been taken into account by firms.
options.B: GDP greatly overstates the true value of output because some of the profit it includes is supernormal profit.
options.C: GDP is a better measure of living standards than GNP because net property income from abroad is not available for citizens.
options.D: GNP per capita ignores many important factors that affect citizens’ living standards.

questions.questionText: The chart provides information about employment rates, as a percentage of total employment, in the primary, secondary and tertiary sector of four countries. What is most likely to represent the most economically developed country? % of total employment key primary sector secondary sector tertiary sector

options.A: B C D country

questions.questionText: A government is committed to increasing real GDP using only fiscal and monetary policies. Which combination of measures is likely to be the most effective in achieving this aim? fiscal policy monetary policy

options.A: increase in the budget deficit central bank buys back government bonds
options.B: increased government spending on roads increased short term rate of interest
options.C: reduce income taxes central bank sells more government bonds
options.D: reduce wealth taxes increase commercial banks’ cash deposit ratio

questions.questionText: What describes the multiplier process, as it operates within a closed economy with no government sector?

options.A: Changes in National Income determine the level of investment.
options.B: The level of consumption depends on the level of National Income.
options.C: The levels of consumption and investment together determine the level of National Income.
options.D: When investment changes, there will be a greater change in equilibrium National Income.

questions.questionText: In an economy with no government sector:

options.C: = consumption I = investment X = exports M = imports Y = national income. If C = 40 + 0.5Y, I = 80, X = 100 and M = 100, what will be the equilibrium level of Y?

questions.questionText: Which policy does a central bank undertake to pursue quantitative easing?

options.A: purchase long-term government debt from the public
options.B: purchase short-term government debt from the public
options.C: sell long-term government debt to the public
options.D: sell short-term government debt to the public

questions.questionText: What would be an increase in leakages or withdrawals from the circular flow of income?

options.A: increase in government spending on anti-smoking campaigns
options.B: increase in spending on imports of luxury cars
options.C: increase in spending on transfer payments
options.D: increase in wages paid to government employees

questions.questionText: Which statement would both Keynesian and Monetarist schools of thought accept?

options.A: High inflation and high unemployment are undesirable in a properly-functioning economy.
options.B: Increased government spending on investment projects will always crowd out private investment.
options.C: The best way for an economy to get out of a recession is for the government to increase its expenditure.
options.D: The most effective way to reduce inflation is for the government to exercise tight control over the money supply.

questions.questionText: In country X the marginal rate of income tax imposed on the highest earners was 83% which increased to 98% if income was received from interest or dividends. The highest marginal rate was then reduced to 40%. Despite this reduction, the tax revenue raised from the highest earners increased substantially. Which theoretical concept illustrates this relationship between tax rates and tax revenue?

options.A: the J curve
options.B: the Laffer curve
options.C: the Marshall-Lerner condition
options.D: the Phillips curve

questions.questionText: A government is increasing the role of market forces in its economy. However, it imposed temporary maximum price controls. Why might a government, committed to reducing central planning, introduce price controls?

options.A: to increase allocative efficiency
options.B: to increase the incentive for producers to raise supply
options.C: to reduce consumer demand
